content: Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of isosorbide mononitrate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Ketoconazole decreases the levels of rifampin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both drugs are administered orally. The clinical significance remains unclear. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin increases the effects of leflunomide by enhancing its metabolism, specifically through its active metabolite. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Levoketoconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs, and its clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of levothyroxine by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of liothyronine by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of lisinopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or effects of loratadine by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of meloxicam by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Miconazole vaginal formulation decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs, and its clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of modafinil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of moexipril by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of morphine by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of nevirapine by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of nortriptyline by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or effects of ondansetron by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of opium tincture by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of oxacillin by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of perindopril by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of pirmenol by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of piroxicam by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Posaconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs, and its clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of quinapril by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or effects of rabeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of ramelteon by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of ramipril by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of riluzole by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pyrazinamide reduces the levels of tacrolimus through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of abemaciclib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is necessary, close monitoring is required. Rifampin decreases the levels of abiraterone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. If unavoidable, the abiraterone dosage frequency should be increased from once daily to twice daily. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of abrocitinib by enhancing its metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP2C9 or CYP2C19 inducers should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. If unavoidable, the acalabrutinib dose should be increased to 200 mg twice daily. Rifampin reduces the levels of acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) by enhancing its metabolism, potentially increasing the levels of hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of adagrasib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the levels of afatinib by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If chronic therapy with a P-gp inducer is required, the afatinib daily dose may be increased by 10 mg as tolerated. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of alfentanil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of aliskiren by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of almotriptan by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of alosetron by inducing hepatic CYP1A2, CYP3A4, and CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of alpelisib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of alprazolam by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the absorption of aluminum hydroxide, magnesium carbonate, and magnesium trisilicate when co-administered. Rifampin should be taken at least 1 hour before antacids to avoid reduced absorption. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of ambrisentan by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration may cause a transient increase in ambrisentan AUC, but no clinically significant effect is observed by day 7. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of amiodarone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of amitriptyline by inducing hepatic CYP2C19, CYP3A4, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of amlodipine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels of amobarbital by enhancing its metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels of ampicillin by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of antipyrine by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Apalutamide reduces the levels of rifampin by increasing its elimination. Apalutamide weakly induces OATP1B1, which may decrease systemic exposure to drugs that are OATP1B1 substrates. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of apixaban by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of apremilast by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP inducers should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of aprepitant by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of aripiprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of armodafinil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced antimalarial efficacy. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of artesunate by inducing UGT enzymes, which may decrease the AUC and peak plasma concentration of its active metabolite (DHA). Close monitoring for reduced efficacy is recommended. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of asenapine by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of atogepant by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring and therapy modification are recommended. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of atorvastatin by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the levels of atovaquone by enhancing its metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of avanafil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, especially in patients with erectile dysfunction. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of avapritinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or effects of avatrombopag by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, especially in patients with ITP. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or effects of axitinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Azithromycin increases the levels of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity.
